title: The unlabelled bridge-addable fragment-size conjecture
source: Colin McDiarmid, “Connectivity for an unlabelled bridge-addable graph class”, arXiv:2001.05256 (2020). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05256), Conjecture 3

lanes.formal_and_paper: bridge-addable-fragment-345190-formal-paper-sol62-20261119-r1 (GPT-6.2 Sol, 11 modules; construction changed to zero-offset matchings)
lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-345190-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-345190.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used; confirmed the formalized class is non-degenerate and not a standard example)

significance.root_decision: McDiarmid's Conjecture 3 (the expected fragment size of a uniformly random unlabelled n-vertex graph from a decomposable, bridge-addable class is bounded by a universal constant) is false: there is one fixed isomorphism-invariant, decomposable, bridge-addable class of graphs, with members at every positive order, whose mean fragment size over isomorphism classes of n-vertex members is unbounded in n. The class consists of graphs whose bridgeless pieces are single vertices or members of a staged family of cyclic-layer graphs with very many isomorphism types; the bound obtained is of order t^2/6 at stage t. The first stage begins at about 2^86 vertices, so the effect is invisible at any computable size (below 2^85 vertices the class is exactly the forests).
significance.caveat: The formalized class differs in detail from the one in the discovery proof (the paper proves the formalized one; an independent referee re-derived every inequality). The first stage starts near 2^86 vertices, so no direct numerical confirmation at true size is possible; scaled-down copies were checked. The same class refutes the sibling record MathDB 345191 (Conjecture 4), which is not claimed separately. Bounded literature search; both papers citing the source treat the unlabelled conjectures as open.

root_basis: Root extracted the eleven modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee compared the Lean definitions word by word with McDiarmid's text, confirmed that the endpoint is the exact negation of Conjecture 3 with the mean taken over isomorphism classes, checked the changed construction on scaled-down copies with its own isomorphism test and exact arithmetic, read the paper line by line and supplied the revised paper used here.
